links.outcome: Concordance and specificity of GPT-agent versus microbiologists against routine diagnostics
links.effect: Microbiologists concordant in 94.4% of categories vs 81.9% for EUCAST-GPT-expert; humans had higher specificities (ESBL 99.1% vs 69.23%).
links.quote: Microbiologists showed higher concordance and shorter argumentations compared to GPT-agents.

links.outcome: Non-customized GPT-4 ability to interpret resistance categories and agreement with routine diagnostics
links.effect: Non-customized GPT-4 could interpret 169/862 (19.6%) categories; 137/169 (81.1%) agreed with routine diagnostics.
links.quote: Non-customized GPT-4 could interpret 169/862 (19.6%) categories, and 137/169 (81.1%) agreed with routine diagnostics.

unlisted_practices: Customizing a GPT agent with domain guidelines (EUCAST breakpoint tables) to improve accuracy over a non-customized LLM

screen.reason: The study evaluates a customized GPT-agent versus off-the-shelf GPT-4 and human microbiologists on retrospective microbiology data for detecting antimicrobial resistance mechanisms, benchmarking diagnostic accuracy without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
